$comment: A new member's photos waiting for a person (design §2.7, §8.5; ADR-0026 D3; OD-41, decided: every photo is approved by a person before anyone else sees it). The owner sees every state; nobody else sees anything but approved photos, and the storage policy enforces it, not the client. M1-PR3 (photos and the storage policy) and M1-PR4 (the moderator's queue) implement it.

states.processing: Uploaded to meet-inbox; the media worker has not yet stripped metadata, checked the bytes and moved it. No path yet.
states.pending_review: In the moderation queue. Visible to its owner only.
states.rejected: Visible to its owner with the reason, so they can replace it. Reasons: not_a_person, not_you, explicit, contact_details, violence, low_quality, reused, other.
states.removed: Taken down after an upheld case or deleted by the owner; its files are erased. Not returned.
states.failed: The worker could not process it (wrong type, too small, corrupt). Ask for another photo.

quick_win: While the first photo waits: 'Your photos are in review, usually within 12 hours.' Browsing needs an active profile, so show today's question and the ladder until then.

meet_set_discoverable_too_early.note: Turning discovery on needs a clean first name, at least one approved photo and an area.

photo_status_m1.note: A photo status needs photo verification and goes through the same review; a text status goes live after screening.

admin_meet_moderation_queue_row.note: Staff only (meet_moderator, super_admin, in country scope). Priority 1 is child safety or underage, 2 reports with evidence, 3 first-photo pre-moderation, 4 other photos and statuses, 5 text holds. The console reads the image through a signed URL of at most 300 seconds. Labels are illustrative; M1-PR4 fixes them.

never_shown_to_the_owner: Proposed here for M1-PR4 to confirm: that a rejection was for 'underage_appearance'. That decision places a discovery hold and opens a child-safety review (RB-17), and naming it would tell the person what was noticed, so the owner sees reason 'other'.
